source: aban news — kuratiert aus 30 Newsletter-Ausgaben + DACH-Standard-Stack

tools.name: Claude
tools.aban_note: Best conversational AI for German texts. I use it daily for aban news. Sonnet 4.6 is my default, Opus for long research, Haiku for bulk work.
tools.dsgvo_note: EU data residency via the Anthropic API; zero retention on request.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.aban_note: Standard kit. GPT-5 is a solid all-rounder, but for German business texts Claude consistently lands finer. If you only have one tool: this one.

tools.name: Gemini
tools.aban_note: Strong on multimodal + long context. Workspace integration is interesting for Google users. Standalone: second choice against Claude.

tools.name: Mistral Le Chat
tools.aban_note: EU-based (Paris). For compliance-sensitive DACH customers it's now a clean choice. Big clients like BNP, Harvey AI are the trust signal. Codestral for coding is solid.

tools.name: DeepSeek
tools.aban_note: Disruptive pricing (-75 to -99% vs OpenAI). Unbeatable for bulk workloads without compliance worries. For DACH business data I wouldn't route through it - Chinese provider.

tools.name: Perplexity
tools.aban_note: Research tool No. 1. Pro with Sonar models replaces Google for me on 80% of questions. Source transparency is the killer feature.

tools.name: Aleph Alpha (Pharia)
tools.aban_note: German LLMs, Heidelberg. Pharia-1 for regulated industries (pharma, banking, public admin). Performance lags Claude/Mistral - but if your compliance officer wants 'EU-sovereign', it's the answer. No self-service.

tools.name: Claude Cowork
tools.aban_note: Three days of real self-testing (see issue 002). Worth it for PDF analysis, slide decks from briefings, Excel pivots from raw data. I need it twice a week. No miracle tool, but concrete time savings.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.aban_note: Pragmatic multi-model router. Unbeatable for API-cost questions. I ignored it for months - a mistake. Now my default for A/B tests between providers.

tools.name: n8n
tools.aban_note: Self-hostable, GDPR-friendly, German company. My backend for newsletter automation. Make.com is more polished, n8n is more robust and controllable.

tools.name: Make.com
tools.aban_note: Nice visual builder. Faster onboarding than n8n. But: vendor lock-in and pricier at volume. Great for beginners, n8n for pros.

tools.name: Zapier
tools.aban_note: Largest ecosystem (7000+ apps). But expensive and limited in logic. If you only need SaaS-A -> SaaS-B, it works. For AI workflows: Make or n8n.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.aban_note: My default editor. VSCode fork with Claude/GPT integrated. Composer mode is the game-changer for vibecoding. If you write code and don't have Cursor - you're losing time.

tools.name: Windsurf
tools.aban_note: Cursor rival. Cascade mode is conceptually cleaner. Tried it, but the Cursor workflow sat too deep. Anyone starting fresh: solid pick.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.aban_note: A classic, now with Claude Sonnet as an option. Solid autocomplete. Cursor is superior in agent mode, Copilot in the GitHub integration flow.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.aban_note: Terminal-based coding agent. When you automate routines (refactor 50 files, push up test coverage), it's strong. CLI > GUI for power users.

tools.name: Bolt.new
tools.aban_note: Browser-based vibecoding. A landing page in 20 min. Lock-in & limits as soon as it gets more complex. For MVPs: usable.

tools.name: Lovable
tools.aban_note: Very smooth vibecoding builder. Nice outputs. Scales poorly beyond the first 200 prompts. For solos with just one side project: ok.

tools.name: v0
tools.aban_note: Next.js + shadcn out of the box. If you're in the Vercel ecosystem: first choice. Otherwise: output is React-specific, which is limiting.

tools.name: Replit Agent
tools.aban_note: Full-stack in the browser including hosting. Suited for complete mini-apps. Pricing is harsh at volume.

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.aban_note: Image-quality king. v7 is astonishing. For marketing assets, editorial images, covers. Discord-first is annoying, but the web UI works fine now.

tools.name: Flux
tools.aban_note: German company (Freiburg), the Stable Diffusion makers. Flux.1 Dev is top performance. Open weights - ideal for DACH compliance.

tools.name: Stable Diffusion
tools.aban_note: Open-source classic. Self-hostable. If you have an RTX graphics card: ComfyUI + SD = unlimited images without vendor dependency.

tools.name: Ideogram
tools.aban_note: Best text-in-image rendering. For posters, logos, typography-heavy designs. Weaker on photorealism.

tools.name: Krea
tools.aban_note: Realtime image-gen + multi-model bundle. Interesting for designers because output control is good. Tier 1 is limiting.

tools.name: Recraft
tools.aban_note: SVG generation + brand-style consistency. If you have to keep brand images consistent: top.

tools.name: Leonardo.ai
tools.aban_note: Image-gen with a focus on game assets. Solid UI, but output for marketing is second league.

tools.name: Playground AI
tools.aban_note: The free tier is generous. Output is usually passable, rarely outstanding. Fine for hobby use.

tools.name: DALL-E 3
tools.aban_note: Now overtaken by Midjourney/Flux. But: seamlessly integrated into the ChatGPT workflow. Good enough for quick slide images.

tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.aban_note: Commercial-safe (trained on licensed data). For brands that have to generate legally safely. Seamless in Photoshop/Illustrator.

tools.name: Sora
tools.aban_note: Video-gen. Exciting, but in 2026 not yet production-ready for marketing. Demo clips yes, hero videos no.

tools.name: Runway
tools.aban_note: Gen-4 is solid. Best tool suite for video AI (motion brush, inpainting). For pros who really want to produce.

tools.name: Pika
tools.aban_note: Short-form video for social. Easy onboarding, but output is limited duration.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.aban_note: German voices sound astonishingly natural in 2026. For podcasts, voiceovers, audiobooks. Voice-clone is frighteningly good - with all the ethical implications.

tools.name: Suno
tools.aban_note: Music generation. For jingles, background music, fun. For serious production: the legal situation in DACH is unclear.

tools.name: Udio
tools.aban_note: Suno rival. Similar output quality. Licensing situation just as unclear - careful with commercial use.

tools.name: Murf
tools.aban_note: Solid TTS classic. German voices ok, but ElevenLabs is ahead in 2026.

tools.name: HeyGen
tools.aban_note: AI avatars that read out texts. Translation into 40+ languages with lip-sync. Strong for multi-language marketing. Avatar output stays recognizably synthetic.

tools.name: Synthesia
tools.aban_note: Enterprise AI avatars. Nice templates, pricier than HeyGen. More for L&D departments than solos.

tools.name: D-ID
tools.aban_note: Photo-to-talking-head. Low barrier to entry. Output is now overtaken by HeyGen.

tools.name: Descript
tools.aban_note: Audio/video editing via transcript. Game-changer for podcasters - you delete words in the text, the audio follows. Voice-clone (Overdub) is clean.

tools.name: VEED
tools.aban_note: Browser video editing with AI helpers. Subtitle generation is good. Too limited for power editing.

tools.name: CapCut
tools.aban_note: Mobile-first editing with AI features. It's the built-in tool for the TikTok pipeline. Privacy concerns: ByteDance.

tools.name: Otter.ai
tools.aban_note: Classic for meeting transcripts. German okay, not perfect. For English meetings: first-rate.

tools.name: Fireflies
tools.aban_note: Like Otter, with better CRM sync. German models similarly okay. More customer-friendly pricing.

tools.name: Granola
tools.aban_note: My new default. No bot in the meeting - it runs in the background on your Mac. Notes output for German meetings is first-class. It's replaced Otter.

tools.name: tl;dv
tools.aban_note: German company (Munich). Good multi-language performance. Bot-in-meeting workflow, which Granola solves more elegantly.

tools.name: Krisp
tools.aban_note: Noise cancellation for calls. Works in an unfussy, reliable way. Built-in AI meeting notes since 2025.

tools.name: Fathom
tools.aban_note: Generous free tier with unlimited meetings. US-focused, German language quality ok.

tools.name: DeepL
tools.aban_note: German company (Cologne). Best DE<->EN translation, period. Write is a Grammarly rival - solid for German. A Pro account is standard kit for every DACH solo.

tools.name: DeepL Write
tools.aban_note: Clearly better than Grammarly for German. Style adjustment 'Business', 'Academic', 'Casual' works. 14-day test in issue 017.

tools.name: Grammarly
tools.aban_note: English refiner. Too weak for German texts - take DeepL Write or LanguageTool. For English outreach: ok.

tools.name: LanguageTool
tools.aban_note: German company (Potsdam). Open-source core. Stronger than the Duden corrector for German style issues. Self-hostable.

tools.name: Tavily
tools.aban_note: Search API for AI agents. If your agents need web research, Tavily is the clean default. Cheaper than SerpAPI.

tools.name: Exa
tools.aban_note: Semantic-search API. Finds thematically similar content better than keyword search. Ideal for research agents.

tools.name: You.com
tools.aban_note: AI search + modes for code, research. Perplexity is the better choice in 2026, You still has a niche.

tools.name: Phind
tools.aban_note: Search for devs. Code-focused answers with sources. Usable as a Stack Overflow replacement.

tools.name: Kagi
tools.aban_note: Paid search without ads, with AI assist. Refreshing for power searchers. Costs money, but worth it if you Google daily.

tools.name: Brave Search
tools.aban_note: Own index. Privacy-first. AI summary integrated. Solid Google alternative without tracking.

tools.name: Groq
tools.aban_note: Inference-speed champion. Llama, Mixtral at insane tokens/s. If you build latency-sensitive apps: first choice.

tools.name: Together AI
tools.aban_note: Open-source models (Llama, Mixtral, Qwen) as an API. Cheap inference, good model selection.

tools.name: Cerebras Inference
tools.aban_note: Custom chips, very fast inference. Llama hosting is top. Model selection more limited than Groq.

tools.name: Replicate
tools.aban_note: Host open-source models as an API. Incl. image/audio/video models. Good for prototyping.

tools.name: Hugging Face
tools.aban_note: GitHub for AI models. Inference endpoints are solid. The Datasets library is gold for researchers.

tools.name: LangChain
tools.aban_note: Framework for LLM apps. Polarizing: many find it over-engineered. Ok for standard patterns, for custom logic better write directly.

tools.name: LlamaIndex
tools.aban_note: RAG framework. Leaner than LangChain for retrieval use cases. For doc-search applications, the clean choice.

tools.name: Weaviate
tools.aban_note: EU-based vector DB. Netherlands, GDPR-compliant. Production-ready. Open-source core.

tools.name: Qdrant
tools.aban_note: German vector DB (Berlin). Open-source. Self-hostable. Performance is top. First choice for DACH RAG setups.

tools.name: Pinecone
tools.aban_note: Managed vector DB. US-only cloud. Convenient, but lock-in. For DACH compliance: take Qdrant.

tools.name: Chroma
tools.aban_note: Lean vector DB for local dev and small prototypes. Production: switch to Qdrant.

tools.name: Notion AI
tools.aban_note: If you live in Notion, it's worth it. Q&A over the workspace is okay. For outside-of-Notion workflows: not worth it.

tools.name: Mem
tools.aban_note: Notes app with built-in AI. Auto-tagging and semantic search work well. The mobile app is solid.

tools.name: Reflect
tools.aban_note: Notes app with GPT-4 integrated. Very clean. Daily notes + backlinks like Roam, with AI on top.

tools.name: Obsidian
tools.aban_note: Local-first, plain Markdown. With plugins (Copilot, Smart Connections) it becomes AI-capable. My second brain for 4 years.

tools.name: Loom
tools.aban_note: Screen recording with AI transcript + summary. Worth its weight in gold for async updates to clients. The free tier is enough for solos.

tools.name: Cap.so
tools.aban_note: Open-source Loom alternative. EU hosting possible. Interesting for DACH data protection.

tools.name: Jasper
tools.aban_note: Marketing-writing tool. Was hot in 2023, now overtaken by Claude/ChatGPT. Templates are no longer a killer feature.

tools.name: Copy.ai
tools.aban_note: Workflow focus now. Usable for sales teams without AI skills. Solo marketer: Claude is enough.

tools.name: Writesonic
tools.aban_note: Content-gen tool. Mediocre outputs, Claude is better. Chatsonic is its own chat - ChatGPT is better.

tools.name: Sudowrite
tools.aban_note: Fiction-writing AI. Specialized for novelists. English-first, German ok.

tools.name: Lex
tools.aban_note: AI-augmented text editor. Inline AI calls on selections. Nice distraction-free UI.

tools.name: Wordtune
tools.aban_note: Sentence rewriting. English-first. Too weak for German.

tools.name: QuillBot
tools.aban_note: Paraphrasing + grammar. Strong in English. Plagiarism check is a nice bonus.

tools.name: Anyword
tools.aban_note: Marketing copy with performance scoring. English-first. Expensive for solos.

tools.name: Profound
tools.aban_note: Generative-engine-optimization tracking. Measures whether your brand shows up in ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity. In 2026 it's what Google ranking was in 2010.

tools.name: AthenaHQ
tools.aban_note: GEO-tracking competitor to Profound. Mid-market pricing. Reports in German ok.

tools.name: Otterly
tools.aban_note: Austrian company (Vienna). DACH-language-first. The affordable GEO entry point for SMEs.

tools.name: Ahrefs
tools.aban_note: SEO standard. Backlinks, keywords, site audit. AI features are a side dish, the index is the value.

tools.name: SEMrush
tools.aban_note: Broader toolset than Ahrefs (also ad intel). Pricier. If you do both: SEMrush.

tools.name: Surfer SEO
tools.aban_note: On-page SEO optimizer with AI writing. Content-score optimization works well for English content, German okay.

tools.name: Frase
tools.aban_note: SEO content-brief generator. Cheaper than Surfer. Solid tool for content marketers.

tools.name: MarketMuse
tools.aban_note: Topic-cluster strategy for enterprise content. Overkill for solos.

tools.name: Canva
tools.aban_note: Magic Studio turns Canva into an AI design platform. The most pragmatic design tool for DACH solos. Templates + AI = fast to usable output.

tools.name: Figma AI
tools.aban_note: AI features in Figma (Make Designs, Make Prototype) are solid. The standard for UI design.

tools.name: Gamma
tools.aban_note: AI slides from text. Nicer than Decktopus, faster than PowerPoint+AI. Usable for pitch decks.

tools.name: Beautiful.ai
tools.aban_note: Smart templates with auto-layout. Solid, but not outstanding.

tools.name: Ollama
tools.aban_note: Local LLMs on Mac/PC. Llama, Mistral, Qwen locally. If GDPR is strict: your friend. Hardware-hungry.

tools.name: LM Studio
tools.aban_note: GUI for local LLMs. Nicer onboarding than the Ollama CLI. Server mode for API calls from your own apps.

tools.name: Open WebUI
tools.aban_note: ChatGPT clone for Ollama. Self-hosted. If your team needs local AI: this is it.

tools.name: Lingo.dev
tools.aban_note: Localization for software strings. AI-translates JSON/i18n files. Useful for multi-lang apps.

tools.name: Browserbase
tools.aban_note: Headless-browser cloud for AI agents. If your agent has to operate websites: solid infra.

tools.name: Browse AI
tools.aban_note: Visual scraper. Click on fields, AI extracts. For list-building & monitoring.

tools.name: Apify
tools.aban_note: EU-based (Czechia). Largest scraper library. Power-user tool for data pipelines.

tools.name: Bardeen
tools.aban_note: Browser automation for knowledge workers. Basically Zapier for your browser. AI playbooks are nice.

tools.name: Clay
tools.aban_note: Sales intelligence + enrichment. Power tool for lead-gen teams. Expensive, but when it works - money back in a week.

tools.name: Apollo.io
tools.aban_note: Sales database + outreach suite. Good for DACH when used thoughtfully - data quality in Germany fluctuates.

tools.name: Lusha
tools.aban_note: Contact enrichment. GDPR problems documented - be careful. Ok for US data.

tools.name: Intercom Fin
tools.aban_note: Support AI agent. 50% auto-resolution possible. Expensive per resolution, but the math works out for volume support.

tools.name: Zendesk AI
tools.aban_note: AI add-on on Zendesk. If you have Zendesk anyway: activate it. Standalone value: meh.

tools.name: Aider
tools.aban_note: Terminal coding agent. Git-aware, multi-file. Open-source. The clean alternative to Cursor for power users.

tools.name: Cline
tools.aban_note: VSCode extension agent. Plan + Act modes. Very well thought out. Open-source.

tools.name: Tabnine
tools.aban_note: Privacy-first code completion. Self-hostable for enterprise. Interesting for compliance-heavy companies.

tools.name: Sourcegraph Cody
tools.aban_note: Codebase-aware AI for large repos. If you have a monorepo: strong. Solo: Cursor is enough.

tools.name: Warp
tools.aban_note: AI terminal. Agent mode can do multi-step shell tasks. Nice UI. Cloud sync - mind your privacy.

tools.name: GPT Codex
tools.aban_note: OpenAI's coding agent. Cloud-based. Works, but Claude Code in the terminal is more rounded.

tools.name: Pipedream
tools.aban_note: Code + no-code hybrid. For devs who want to write workflows in JavaScript.

tools.name: Windmill
tools.aban_note: Self-hosted workflow engine. EU-based (Paris). When n8n is too limited and you want code.

tools.name: Supabase
tools.aban_note: Open-source Firebase. EU hosting. pgvector included. Backend kit for solo devs.

tools.name: Vercel AI SDK
tools.aban_note: AI SDK for TypeScript. Cleaner than LangChain for standard use cases. If you do Next.js: first choice.

tools.name: Modal
tools.aban_note: Serverless GPU compute. For custom model deployment without infrastructure stress.

tools.name: Linear
tools.aban_note: Issue tracker with AI features (auto-triage, summary). My tool for side projects. The UI is in a class of its own.

tools.name: Humata
tools.aban_note: PDF Q&A tool. Now overtaken by Claude/ChatGPT PDF upload.

tools.name: Consensus
tools.aban_note: AI search over scientific papers. Gold for fact research beyond LinkedIn-level knowledge.

tools.name: Elicit
tools.aban_note: Research workflow for scientific literature. Auto-extraction of findings. Clearly better than ChatGPT for researchers.

tools.name: Scite.ai
tools.aban_note: Citation validation. Shows whether papers are supported or refuted. For serious research.

tools.name: Tactiq
tools.aban_note: Browser-based meeting AI. Cheap, ok output. Granola clearly beats it.

tools.name: Castmagic
tools.aban_note: Podcast-to-content. Generates show notes, quotes, tweets from audio. For podcasters.

tools.name: Pictory
tools.aban_note: Text-to-video from blog posts. Output is recognizably AI-generated. Fine for bulk social snippets.

tools.name: Lumen5
tools.aban_note: Blog-to-social-video. Template-driven. Output is enough for LinkedIn posts, no more.

tools.name: Whisper Flow
tools.aban_note: Voice-to-text dictation for Mac. Faster than typing. German recognition is first-class.

tools.name: Raycast AI
tools.aban_note: Spotlight replacement with AI calls everywhere in the OS. Quick-prompt workflow without switching to the browser. Mac-only.

tools.name: Arc Search
tools.aban_note: Mobile browser with AI summary. 'Browse for me' is nice. A pivot to Dia is coming.

tools.name: Dia (Browser)
tools.aban_note: AI-first browser. Cross-tab chat. Interesting concept, beta status.

tools.name: Klue
tools.aban_note: Competitive-intelligence platform. Enterprise pricing. For solos: too big.

tools.name: Crayon
tools.aban_note: Competitive tracking. Like Klue. Enterprise.

tools.name: Glean
tools.aban_note: Enterprise search over all SaaS tools. A killer for teams > 50 people. Solo setup: overkill.

tools.name: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
tools.aban_note: Open standard for tool-calling. Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, everyone is adopting it. If you build tools for agents: this is it.

tools.name: Together Code Interpreter
tools.aban_note: Code-execution sandbox as an API. For agents that have to run code.

tools.name: E2B
tools.aban_note: Sandbox infrastructure for AI agents. EU-based (Prague). Open-source core. Clean choice for agent builders.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.aban_note: German LLM-observability platform (Berlin). Tracing, eval, cost-tracking. Self-hostable. When your LLM stack gets serious: first choice.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.aban_note: LLM observability for LangChain apps. Vendor-lock-light. Cloud-only EU region not until 2026.

tools.name: browser-use
tools.aban_note: Python library for AI browser control. Open-source. Lean stack for agent builders.

tools.name: Poe
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Poe bundles several AI models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.) in one interface and lets you build your own chatbots.

tools.name: NotebookLM
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Analyzes uploaded documents and answers only based on your own sources, incl. automatic podcast summaries.

tools.name: Fellow
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] AI meeting assistant with agendas, automatic notes, action items and 1-on-1 tools.

tools.name: Avoma
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Transcribes meetings, creates AI notes and updates CRM entries, focused on sales teams.

tools.name: Readwise Reader
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Read-it-later for articles, PDFs and newsletters with AI summaries and highlight sync.

tools.name: Tana
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Agent-based meeting and knowledge workspace with live transcription and context diagram.

tools.name: Napkin AI
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Automatically turns text into infographics, diagrams and flowcharts.

tools.name: Komo Search
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Ad-free AI search engine with generative answers and source citations, without user tracking.

tools.name: Lindy
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Personal AI assistant that manages emails, records meetings and handles calendar-based tasks.

tools.name: Spinach AI
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Automates agile standups and meeting notes and syncs action items with Jira, GitHub and Slack.

tools.name: Le Chat (Mistral)
tools.dsgvo_note: EU provider (France), data stays within the EU.
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Mistral's European AI assistant with web search, code interpreter and canvas editor, GDPR-relevant as an EU provider.

tools.name: Coda AI
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Unites documents, tables and automations with built-in AI for texts, summaries and formulas.

tools.name: Goblin Tools
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Free collection of small AI helpers, incl. breaking large tasks into small steps, built for neurodivergent people.

tools.name: mymind
tools.dsgvo_note: Private, no tracking, no reselling of user data.
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Private AI storage for bookmarks, notes and images with automatic tagging and semantic search.

tools.name: Freepik AI Suite
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] AI image generator and creative platform with many image and video models plus an editing suite.

tools.name: Magnific AI
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] AI image upscaler that scales up photos and AI images and reconstructs details.

tools.name: Topaz Photo AI
tools.dsgvo_note: Local desktop software, no cloud upload.
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Local software for AI photo enhancement with noise reduction, sharpening and upscaling.

tools.name: Topaz Video AI
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Local software for AI video optimization: upscaling to 4K, frame interpolation, stabilization.

tools.name: Luma Dream Machine
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] AI video generator that creates videos with camera movements from text and image prompts.

tools.name: Kling AI
tools.dsgvo_note: Provider in China (Kuaishou); data-protection review recommended.
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] AI video generator with realistic motion physics and a free entry tier for short clips.

tools.name: Hailuo AI
tools.dsgvo_note: Provider in China (MiniMax); data-protection review recommended.
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Fast AI video generator that turns text and images into short 1080p videos.

tools.name: Cartesia AI
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Real-time TTS API with low latency and voice cloning, for developers and product teams.

tools.name: Wondercraft AI
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Turns scripts into fully produced podcast episodes with AI voices, music and sound effects.

tools.name: OpusClip
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Automatically cuts long videos into short clips for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, with subtitles.

tools.name: Submagic
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] AI tool for animated subtitles on short videos in many languages with keyword highlighting.

tools.name: Vizard AI
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Automatically slices webinars and podcasts into social-media clips with subtitles.

tools.name: AdCreative.ai
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Generates performance-optimized image and video ads from brand assets for social and display campaigns.

tools.name: Gumloop
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] No-code AI automation with a visual node editor for data processing and lead generation.

tools.name: Relay.app
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] AI workflow automation that combines AI actions, logic and human approvals in a visual editor.

tools.name: Dust
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Platform to build specialized AI agents with access to internal data sources (Slack, Notion, CRM).

tools.name: Zed
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Fast AI code editor in Rust with a built-in AI assistant and collaborative editing.

tools.name: Devin
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] Autonomous AI software engineer that plans, writes, debugs and deploys code.

tools.name: Systeme.io
tools.aban_note: [Editorial: review & rate] All-in-one platform for online business: sales funnels, email marketing, courses and automation in one tool, with a generous free plan.
